findings.title: One failed SendGrid cancel aborts the whole cancellation batch and skips DB cleanup
findings.body: The cancellation loop runs inside a single try block. The query at lines 44-51 does not filter on referenceId or scheduled, so a cancelled reminder that was never scheduled in SendGrid (referenceId null) is sent to /v3/user/scheduled_sends with batch_id null, which throws. The catch then exits the loop, so every later reminder in the batch is not cancelled in this run and is still sent. Also, the prisma.workflowReminder.delete promises already pushed to workflowRemindersToDelete are never awaited because the Promise.all at line 74 is skipped, so rows for reminders that were successfully cancelled are not deleted. Each cancellation should be handled individually and the query should filter on referenceId not null.

findings.title: Cancellations requested close to send time can still be delivered
findings.body: The cron only picks up cancelled reminders when scheduledDate is within the next hour and it runs every 15 minutes. A reminder cancelled shortly before its send time (e.g. 10 minutes out) will not be picked up until the next cron run, which can be after the email has already been sent by SendGrid. The window or the cron interval should be tightened, or the cancellation should also be applied immediately when the send time is near.

findings.title: Non-immediate cancel only flags the row, so the SendGrid email is not cancelled now
findings.body: For reminders that already have a referenceId and are not immediateDelete, the function only sets cancelled=true. The SendGrid scheduled send is left untouched until the cron job runs, which may be up to 15+ minutes later and can be after the reminder time. Any caller that expects a cancelled booking to stop emails (handleCancelBooking, bookings.tsx requestReschedule, workflows.tsx step/event-type edits) is therefore relying on the cron timing, and this is not reflected in those call sites.

findings.title: Commented-out testAction block has mismatched comment delimiters, leaving live code that references undefined identifiers
findings.body: The `*/` at the end of line 901 closes the outer `/* testAction` comment that starts at line 848, and the `/*) {` on the same line opens a new comment that is closed only at line 1010. The code between (lines 902-967) is therefore live but refers to identifiers that are no longer imported in this file (dayjs, BookingInfo, getErrorFromUnknown). The `if (` on line 964 is also left without a body. This is unrelated to the PR's reminder logic, and the reindent in this diff makes the hazard harder to see. The block should be properly commented out or removed.

findings.title: Prisma import is now unused
findings.body: After removing deleteReminderPromise, `Prisma` (line 9) is no longer referenced in this file, which will trip lint/typecheck with unused-import rules. The value-style import of the type-only `PrismaPromise` is also inconsistent with the rest of the file.

findings.title: Unrelated UI restructuring changes rendering for SMS_ATTENDEE steps
findings.body: The wrapper condition changed from (isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) to isPhoneNumberNeeded, and the phone block now renders its own container. This is not part of the stated reminder cancellation fix. For SMS_ATTENDEE steps, the previously rendered padded wrapper is now gone, a visible change that is not described or tested.

findings.title: New cancelled column is nullable with no default
findings.body: The column is added as nullable with no default, so existing and newly created rows carry NULL rather than false. Queries and code that treat the flag as a boolean (`cancelled: true` filter, and the schema type Boolean?) must now handle three states. A NOT NULL column with default false would avoid this ambiguity.

findings.title: No tests cover the new cancellation flow
findings.body: The PR changes reminder cancellation semantics across the cron job, booking cancel, reschedule, and workflow edit/delete paths, but adds no tests. There is no coverage for a cancelled reminder that is not yet scheduled, a batch with one failing cancel, or the cancel-within-one-hour window. These are the scenarios that caused the original bug.
